title: Test harness ignores ui.quit(): scripted runs can't test or assert a game's Quit
body:
## Summary

Under `JUDAS_TEST_SCRIPT`, a game calling `ui.quit()` has no effect. The run keeps going until `FRAMES` is reached, and nothing records that a quit was requested. A game's Quit button (or save-then-quit flow) therefore can't be tested automatically.

## Current behaviour (Alpha v1.0.4, `e2008d1e`)

- **Interactive loop:** `src/Application.cpp` stops on quit: `while (!window.ShouldClose() && !play.QuitRequested())`. `ui.quit()` sets that flag through `RuntimeUI::RequestQuit()` (`src/ScriptBindingsUI.cpp`).
- **Harness loop:** `src/TestHarness.cpp` runs `for(int frame=0;frame<script.frames;++frame)` and never checks `QuitRequested()`.
- **Hinge case:** clicking the pause menu's QUIT (by `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP`) logged that the game called `ui.quit()`, but the harness kept rendering. A screenshot 340 frames later still showed the pause menu.

## Request

Either or both:

- **End the run on quit:** stop the harness when a quit is requested and report the frame, e.g. `[TestHarness] quit requested at frame N`. Exit 0, so tests don't depend on the frame budget.
- **An assertion:** e.g. `EXPECT_QUIT <frame>` (and maybe `EXPECT_NO_QUIT`), so a script can check that Quit happened by a given frame. It could also check that pending saves finished first, if quitting is made to wait for them (see #26).

## Notes

- Desktop testing only; device behaviour isn't affected.
- Found while building the Hinge sample game.

title: Saves: small saves wait ~60 frames "queued" before capture (~90 frames total)
body:
## Summary

A small save spends most of its time in the `queued` state before capture starts, so "save, then leave" takes about a second. The docs say capture happens "at a later safe frame boundary" (`docs/judasjs/saves.md`). The measured wait seems longer than the capture and write themselves need.

## Measurements (Hinge, Alpha v1.0.4 `e2008d1e`, desktop Release, Xvfb + llvmpipe, test harness at its default fixed step)

`saves.status(token).state` was logged every `uiUpdate` after `saves.save('hinge_profile', …)`. The slot is about 68 KB; one level scene with roughly 300 entities.

| | `queued` | `writing` | Total to `completed` |
|---|---|---|---|
| World running | ~45–60 frames | ~45 frames | ~90–105 frames |
| World paused by a modal UI document | ~75 frames | ~15 frames | 91 frames |

For the same save, the completed status reports `captureMs` ≈ 13 ms and `workerMs` ≈ 3 ms. The actual work is under 20 ms; most of the wall time is spent waiting.

A save requested while the pause menu is open does complete, so this isn't a hang. It's latency.

## Why it matters

- **Leaving a level takes about a second.** Combined with the "busy" rule (separate issue), every scene change after a save waits that long. Hinge now shows "Saving…" in its menu for about a second when you leave a level.
- **Async state is visible for longer.** Anything waiting on a save, such as a level-select refresh or Continue, waits too.

## Request

- **Investigate the queued interval:** why a small save waits about 60 frames for its capture boundary. Possibly it waits for a specific step or sync point that's rare under a fixed-step harness or when paused.
- **If the wait is deliberate:** a documented "save as soon as possible" option would help. So would documenting the expected latency in `saves.md`.

## Notes

- Measured on desktop with the test harness. Phone timing not measured.
- Found while building the Hinge sample game.

title: Saves/scenes: add a busy query, or let scene changes and loads queue behind a pending save
body:
## Summary

Only one save/scene operation runs at a time, and a conflicting request throws "busy" (`docs/judasjs/saves.md`). That's reasonable, but the JS API gives no way to ask whether the service is busy. A project can only poll `saves.status(token)` for requests it made itself. "Save, then leave the level" is a very common pattern, so every game ends up writing its own queue: track every save token, defer `scenes.load` / `scenes.reload` / `saves.load` / `ui.quit`, and retry on "busy".

## Real case (Hinge, Alpha v1.0.4)

Hinge saves a level slot at checkpoints and a profile slot a few seconds after coins are collected, so a save can be in flight at almost any moment. Every menu action that leaves the level failed whenever it coincided with a save:

```
onUI: TypeError: Scene/save lifecycle is busy
    at load (judas:369:136)
```

- **Affected actions:** NEXT LEVEL, RESTART, MAIN MENU, CONTINUE and QUIT.
- **Hinge's workaround:** its own save queue plus a deferred scene change, retried every `uiUpdate` until the queue is empty and the call no longer throws "busy".
- **Earlier occurrence:** the same pattern was needed earlier for `saves.refresh()` right after a level-start save.

## Request

Either would remove the boilerplate:

1. **A busy query:** a global `saves.busy` (or `saves.idle`), true while any save/load/refresh or scene operation is queued or running. Then projects can wait without tracking every token.
2. **Queueing instead of throwing:** let `scenes.load`, `scenes.reload` and `saves.load` accept a request while a save is pending and run it when the save completes. They could return a token, like `saves.*`, rather than throwing. An explicit option such as `{ afterPendingSaves: true }` would keep today's strict behaviour as the default.

Option 2 also makes "save, then quit" safe if `ui.quit()` can wait for pending writes.

## Notes

- Documented behaviour, so this is an API ergonomics enhancement.
- Related: save latency (separate issue) makes the window in which these calls fail about a second long.

title: JudasJS: one exception in a UI callback silently faults the whole script slot (game becomes unresponsive)
body:
## Summary

When a script callback throws, the script's whole slot (the running instance of the script) is faulted, as documented ("Errors fault slots", `docs/judasjs/practices.md`). For gameplay scripts that also handle UI, one bad click leaves the game visibly running but dead: every later `onUI`, `uiUpdate`, `fixedUpdate` and similar callback stops. Nothing on screen says why. The cause is only in stderr.

## Real case (Hinge, Alpha v1.0.4)

The pause menu's MAIN MENU handler started a `saves.save(...)` and then called `scenes.load(...)` in the same `onUI` call. The load threw, as documented, because a save was in flight:

```
script asset=… entity=1 slot=1 onUI: TypeError: Scene/save lifecycle is busy
    at load (judas:369:136)
    at onUI (Assets/scripts/game.js:1120:20)
```

From then on, no pause menu button responded. The operator reported it on a phone as "the buttons in the pause menu don't work"; nothing on the device pointed at the real cause. The game-side bug is fixed. This issue is about how much damage one uncaught exception does, and how invisible it is.

## Request

Any of these would have made it obvious or survivable:

- **Visible fault in development builds:** when a slot faults, show an on-screen notice in Experimental/Alpha development builds: script, callback, message, first stack frame.
- **Per-callback isolation for UI events:** let an exception in `onUI` fail that one event (logged) instead of faulting the slot, possibly as an opt-in.
- **Queryable fault state:** e.g. a `scripts.faults()` API or an entity-level `scriptFault` field, so a project or the test harness can detect and report a dead slot.

## Notes

- Behaviour as documented. This is a robustness and diagnosability enhancement, not a correctness bug.
- Found while building the Hinge sample game. Test harness repro: open the pause menu while a profile save is in flight and click MAIN MENU.
